about: MUTATING — drops ONE Talos user-volume partition on ONE worker node, destroying the data on it (infra/forge/wipe-a-partition.sh <node> <partition> <plan_sha256>): exactly talosctl -n <the registry's address> wipe disk <partition> --drop-partition, through the forge's ops_talosctl door (the talosconfig David placed, infra/estate/ops-credentials.sh), with the default FAST method. The subcommand and the flag were read from the pinned client's own help: talosctl wipe disk --help of the v1.13.8 talosctl-linux-amd64 that infra/estate/install-cluster-operator.sh pins by sha256, verified against that sha in an uncredentialed build worker on 2026-11-07 (usage 'talosctl wipe disk <device names>... [flags]'; 'Wipe a block device (disk or partition) which is not used as a volume'; --drop-partition: 'drop partition after wipe (if applicable)'; --method FAST or ZEROES, default FAST); Talos itself refuses a device a volume still uses. Asked for by David on 88b35891 and ordered 2026-11-07 ~02:00Z: door 4 of moving w-1's gate volume off the Kingston without a reboot — retire-a-user-volume deletes the UserVolumeConfig, this drops its u-gate partition (Talos provisions a user volume anew only where no partition carries its label), node-converge applies the then-ABSENT entry, prove-gate-volume proves it. The most destructive verb after commission-a-disk, and shaped on it and on shutdown-node. AUTHORISED PER RUN BY DAVID'S PASSKEY in design 17835005's shape: it declares requires_approval with the read-only plan-a-partition-wipe (this script's --plan) as its plan_verb, so the runner renders the plan onto the request's approve step, runs this only after a passkey on the approvers list signs those bytes, and hands the script sha256 of the SIGNED plan; the script re-renders and wipes nothing unless today's plan hashes to it. The plan names the partition by kernel name AND by what Talos says it is — its parent disk's model, serial and wwid, its size, label, index, partition uuid, filesystem and filesystem uuid — so a disk renumbered under the same name hashes differently. THE BOUND IS THE SCRIPT'S, NEVER A PARAM, and every line refuses (exit 78, nothing done): a talos-worker in the live estate registry that the cluster agrees on (a control plane is refused before any door opens); one NVMe partition's kernel name (^nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+p[0-9]+$), never a whole disk; not on the system disk (Talos's systemdisk, or the disk EPHEMERAL lives on); discovered by Talos as a partition labelled u-<name>; its disk carries no other partition; no volume Talos holds owns it (volumestatus: its label, its location, or anything living on its disk); nothing mounted from its disk (talosctl mounts); /var/mnt/<name> not a Longhorn disk (nodes.longhorn.io spec.disks). Every read fails closed (exit 1). THE EFFECT IS READ BACK: every 5 s for up to 120 s, Talos's discoveredvolumes and disks; only when the partition is no longer discovered, no partition on its disk carries its index or partition uuid, and the disk is still there under the same serial is the effect line printed, and otherwise the run exits 1 saying it is NOT proven gone. A second run of an applied plan re-renders to a refusal (nothing to wipe): at most once. Timeout 300: the reads, a wipe bounded at 60 s inside its container, and the 120 s read-back, before the runner's kill.
